summary: Reorganizes channel samples by transposing, sequencing channels into longer channels, or splitting samples into channels.

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Off, swap channels/samples, sequence, or split mode

key_params.name: nval
key_params.note: N value for grouped/every-Nth sequence or split modes

key_params.name: firstsample
key_params.note: Use only the first sample of each channel

key_concepts: Shuffle CHOP reorganizes samples across a set of channels rather than simply renaming or reordering channels.
Swap Channels and Samples transposes the channel/sample layout.
Sequence modes concatenate channels by name, all channels, groups of N, or every Nth channel.
Split modes create numbered channels from samples or sample groups.
Shuffle CHOP is useful after SOP to CHOP or TOP to CHOP when point or image data needs row/column reshaping.
common_gotchas: Swap mode transposes channel/sample layout: many channels can become many samples or the reverse.
Sequencing all channels produces one long channel, which can change downstream assumptions about channel count.
Split modes create numbered channels from sample segments.
Useful after SOP to CHOP or TOP to CHOP when point/image data needs row/column reshaping.
Use Reorder CHOP when only channel order should change; Shuffle CHOP changes sample organization.
